name: Dominion Energy
key_signal: Dominion trades just 2% below its 52-week high on a golden-cross uptrend, but trailing earnings growth is actually negative (-10.2%) and free cash flow remains deeply negative (-$9.9B) even as leverage stays elevated (D/E ~155%).
thesis: Dominion has been re-rated by the market as a prime beneficiary of Virginia's data-center power demand boom, evidenced by price momentum (+20% over 6 months, +15% over 3 months) and a clean technical setup — above both the 50- and 200-day moving averages with a golden cross and MACD confirming the uptrend. Revenue growth of 23% shows the top-line is already responding to load growth, and a low beta (0.64) with a 3.76% dividend yield makes this an attractive holding for income/defensive rotation as rates stabilize. Forward PE of 18.6x is not excessive for a regulated utility with a structural demand tailwind that most peers lack.
bear_case: The fundamentals underneath the rally are shakier than the chart suggests: earnings growth is negative (-10.2%), ROE is a mediocre 9.8%, free cash flow is deeply negative at nearly $10B (reflecting the massive capex needed to serve data-center load, which brings execution and regulatory-lag risk), and debt-to-equity is elevated at 155% — all while the stock sits within 3% of its 52-week high and 12 covering analysts collectively rate it just 'hold.' With RSI at 62 and price already extended well above both moving averages, much of the data-center optionism appears priced in, leaving the stock vulnerable to any capex overrun, rate-case disappointment, or pause in the AI/data-center capex narrative that has driven utility re-ratings sector-wide.
